mode.why: third-party film of unknown origin: borrow the motion language and patterns only, never its shots one by one, its characters' exact design, its copy or its end card (owner note); a voiceover package defaults to REEL. The reference is itself a voiceover reel with UI-card scenes, so UI patterns (glass dashboard, BUY press) are available inside REEL

method: SHA-256 matched meta.json; ffprobe; ffmpeg contact sheets fps=2 (4 sheets, 6x2, all viewed); scene detect gt(scene,0.3) found 3 hard cuts at 7.07, 9.00 and 14.97 s, other shot changes placed from the sheets; dense fps=15 sheets at 2.3–3.3 s (dice → glass-lens reveal) and 18.9–19.9 s (statement → end card). Audio present (voiceover with captions synced phrase by phrase) but not analysed: whether caption changes land on music beats is unverified

visual_language: Light, clean 2.5D glass world: frosted translucent cards, glass-bubble characters with glowing orb heads and simple dot faces, soft spheres and dice, all on a vertical gradient from white light at the top to cobalt at the bottom. Almost everything is code-native (gradients, backdrop blur, CSS 3D tilts, SVG line/area/candle charts, count-up numbers). Typography is two-tier: small geometric-sans captions centred near the top that swap phrase by phrase with the voice (roughly every 0.5–0.9 s), plus a few heavy moments: a huge bold counter, and a giant condensed display headline used once mid-film and once on the end card. Rhythm: 9 shots in 22.5 s (about 2.5 s each), only 3 hard cuts; most changes are camera moves, a pan-off, a glass-lens iris and slides with motion blur. Moves are smooth (ease-in-out, 0.3–2 s), never elastic. Palette is nearly monochrome cobalt; colour itself carries meaning: the scene re-tints to purple then red as risk climbs, and darkens to navy for the low point. Signature moments: the glass-lens iris from the dice into the counter scene, the risk counter changing colour, the camera entering the tilted glass dashboard, the cursor reaching BUY, and the empty-frame pause before the CTA.
continuity: The glass-bubble hero character is the through-line: in the opening group (r1-s1), alone in the counter scene (r1-s3), alone in the dark (r1-s4) and back on the end card (r1-s9).
One background world: the white-top to cobalt-bottom gradient persists in every shot except the deliberate navy low point (r1-s4).
Glass cards are the single UI material: the opening chart card, the crypto cards, the dashboard and the candlestick card are all the same frosted glass.
Charts recur as one motif that grows: a small line (r1-s1) → sparklines (r1-s3) → area waves (r1-s5) → candles (r1-s7).
Colour as state: the whole scene re-tints through one variable (blue → purple → red → navy → back to blue) to show risk and mood.
Captions stay in one fixed slot (top-centre, same size and font) for the whole film, so text never jumps while scenes change.
Round shapes link scenes: the dice and orb heads lead into the circular glass-lens iris, and a big pale sphere sits behind the dashboard.
code_translation: Very code-buildable (estimate 90 %+): CSS gradients, backdrop-filter glass, CSS 3D transforms for card tilts and the camera push, SVG charts, count-up numbers, CSS 3D cube dice, radial-gradient glass characters, a clip-path circle with a refractive ring (blur and highlight) for the lens iris, translate plus blur for slides. Persian adaptation: captions are RTL in the brand font in the same fixed top slot; counters use the brand's digit rule; the giant condensed line maps to the brand's heaviest display weight (no Latin condensed font); slide directions mirror to RTL (text enters from the right).
risks: Third-party film of unknown origin: ADAPT only. Never copy the characters' exact design, the copy, the crypto names, the dollar values, the 'Share this post' card or the shot order one by one.

Reference colours (cobalt, purple, red, navy) map onto brand colour roles: gradient = background role, glass and characters = primary role, counter danger states = the brand's warning/accent roles; never used as literal hex values, and no banned brand colour is introduced by the purple/red risk shift.
Captions swap every 0.5–0.9 s; for Persian, every caption must still meet the minimum hold time, so phrases may be merged; readability wins over pace.
A Latin condensed display face carries the big-type moments; the brand's Persian fonts are not condensed, so the giant line must be shorter (one or two words) to fit the width inside the safe zone.
Light background with thin dark captions: contrast must be checked against the brand's text colour on the white top of the gradient.
Audio not analysed: caption timing in our film comes from our own voice timing (L2), not from the reference.
